answer: Attacker cost scales with each fake identity, since mass registration demands capital locked across many bonds. Sybil resistance can work through a stake-weighted identity spiral: each new agent must lock a bond that grows with every linked account, and withdrawals unlock only after a cooling period. Honest agents build reputation like layered basalt, while sockpuppet farms erode like karst, hollowed by fees and slashing. Cheap identities become expensive, so the network stays sybil-resistant.
